findings.label: Cross-site scripting sinks
findings.method: Searched every source file for dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
findings.detail: 3 file(s) inject raw HTML. 0 of them are outside the reviewed set.
findings.limitation: Finds the sink, not the source. React escapes everything else by default, but this cannot tell whether a value reaching one of these is attacker-controlled.

findings.label: Cross-site request forgery
findings.method: Checked 9 state-changing API route(s) for an origin, referer or CSRF token check.
findings.detail: Every state-changing API route inspects request origin.
findings.limitation: Server actions carry framework CSRF protection and are not counted here. The session cookie is SameSite, which already blocks the cross-site form post this describes, so an unflagged route is not necessarily exploitable.

findings.label: File upload validation
findings.method: Examined 2 route(s) that read request bodies as form data or binary.
findings.detail: Every upload route checks type or size before accepting a file.
findings.limitation: Presence of a check is not correctness of a check. Content sniffing beats an extension test, and this cannot tell which is used.

findings.label: Path traversal
findings.method: Searched for filesystem paths built from request parameters.
findings.detail: No filesystem path is constructed from request input.
findings.limitation: Only direct construction is visible. A request value passed through a variable or helper first would not be matched.

findings.label: Server-side request forgery
findings.method: Searched for outbound fetch calls to a non-literal URL in files that also read request input.
findings.detail: No outbound request is made to a URL that could come from request input.
findings.limitation: Coarse. A file can legitimately do both without the request value reaching the fetch. Treat as a prompt to read the code, not a defect.

findings.label: Password reset flow
findings.method: Looked for a self-service password reset and, if present, whether its tokens expire and are single use.
findings.detail: No self-service password reset exists. Nothing to attack, and nothing for a locked-out administrator either.
findings.limitation: Cannot verify token entropy, or that the reset email goes only to a verified address.

findings.label: Session cookie hardening
findings.method: Read the session cookie options in lib/auth.ts.
findings.detail: httpOnly set, sameSite set, secure set. Lifetime: 60 * 60 * 8.
findings.limitation: Says nothing about session rotation on privilege change, or whether sessions are revoked when an account is disabled.

findings.label: Session signing secret
findings.method: Checked whether the signing secret has a hardcoded fallback and whether production refuses to start without a real one.
findings.detail: Production throws when the secret is absent. A development-only fallback exists and is not reachable in production.
findings.limitation: Cannot judge the strength of the configured secret from here; that is checked at runtime.

findings.label: Rate limiting on public endpoints
findings.method: Checked 6 public state-changing route(s) for a rate limit call.
findings.detail: Every public state-changing route enforces a rate limit.
findings.limitation: Does not evaluate whether the configured limits are appropriate, nor cover server actions.

findings.label: Secrets reaching the browser
findings.method: Looked for secret-shaped NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables, and for server-only environment values read inside client components.
findings.detail: No secret-shaped value is exposed to the browser bundle.
findings.limitation: Judges names, not contents. A secret stored under an innocuous NEXT_PUBLIC_ name would not be caught.

findings.label: Webhook signature verification
findings.method: Looked for inbound webhook routes and whether each verifies a signature.
findings.detail: No inbound webhook endpoint exists, so there is no unsigned webhook to exploit.
findings.limitation: Identifies routes by name. A webhook under a different name would be missed.

findings.label: Object-level authorisation
findings.method: Looked for record lookups keyed on request input that do not also require a session or scope the query to the owner.
findings.detail: Every record lookup driven by request input sits behind a session check or is scoped to the owner.
findings.limitation: The weakest check here. Authorisation can be enforced a layer away, in middleware or a helper, and this only sees one file at a time.

findings.label: Request body validation
findings.method: Checked 6 state-changing route(s) that read a request body for schema validation. Routes with no body are excluded.
findings.detail: Every state-changing route validates its body against a schema.
findings.limitation: Presence of a schema is not the same as a schema that constrains the right things.

findings.label: Sensitive values in logs
findings.method: Searched every log statement for credential-shaped variable names.
findings.detail: No log statement writes a credential-shaped value.
findings.limitation: Matches names. Logging a whole request or user object that happens to contain a secret would not be caught.
